reviews.originalSubtitle: Gate semantics for cross-engine barrier comparisons: |barrier_A − barrier_B| ≤ offset wander, so wander above the 40 meV gate downgrades a VASP-referenced verdict to convention-contaminated.
reviews.subtitle: For the same evaluated configurations, offset wander bounds the difference of sampled energy ranges. Forward barriers need explicit initial states; separately optimized paths also need search-quality and configuration-coverage evidence.
reviews.statement: The historical max-minus-min bound is valid on the same finite set of configurations evaluated by both engines. It describes a sampled energy range. A forward barrier instead subtracts a specified initial energy; shared-initial and separately selected-path comparisons have additional premises.
reviews.reason: The article's broad reuse and clean-gate wording can be read as certifying any cross-engine barrier comparison. Small measured wander does not establish the missing path, initial-state or coverage premises. The July 2026 observations and formalization sketch below remain a historical record; this review does not attribute those observations to a newly demonstrated mechanism.
missingPremises: Match the actual configurations, cells and energy conventions before comparing offsets. Finite sampled images do not establish the unsampled continuous path.
For a forward barrier, name the initial state in each calculation and retain their actual cross-engine initial-energy difference.

For separately selected profiles, bound offsets over a common candidate family and supply each selected profile's gap from that family's minimum peak. Unknown search gaps are not zero; a solver stopping criterion is not a global-optimality certificate.
An energy or scalar-rate bound alone does not certify conductivity or transport. Temperature, prefactors and the applicable transport model remain separate premises.
reviews.bound: For offsets in [a, b] over the common finite candidate family, the forward-barrier difference ΔB = B_G − B_F obeys a − δ₀ − η_F ≤ ΔB ≤ b − δ₀ + η_G. Here δ₀ = G(j) − F(i) uses the actual initial states; η_F and η_G bound the selected peak's gap from its family's minimum peak for each energy function. With a shared initial configuration and zero search gaps, the wander bound is recovered. This remains a finite-family statement, not a global physical-path guarantee.
